coverage: Contact sheets read in full for ch01-s01, ch01-s03, ch02-s01, ch02-s02, ch03-s04, ch04-s03, ch05-s04, ch06-s06, ch08-s05, ch08-s11, ch09-s03, ch10-s04, ch10-s06 and every shot from ch11-s03 to ch15-s10. The other sheets did not load in this session (request limit), so ch01-ch10 were only sampled. Timing was checked against narration/timeline.json word times.

issues.problem: The human silhouettes are generic mannequins with almost no edge detail. Hinton, Bengio, LeCun, Hassabis and the anonymous figures share one body (ch13-s04, ch15-s06, ch13-s03), unlike the reference frame's richly cut costume, hair and props. At a glance the three holdouts cannot be told apart.
issues.fix: In cast.ts give each recurring real person a distinct silhouette signature (hair mass, glasses, beard, posture, height, a period-correct coat cut). Add rim-light edges and 2-3 interior cut lines per figure, as in the reference.

issues.problem: Sets are flatter and plainer than the reference: few ornamental cut-outs, rarely a foreground occluder, and many shots are one mid-plane against a gradient (ch14-s04b, ch15-s05, ch13-s06, ch12-s02). The multiplane depth promised by the brief only shows in about a third of the shots.
issues.fix: Add a shared foreground occluder layer (drapery, chair backs, fretwork, window mullions) and cut-paper filigree to the recurring sets (study, Case Board, candle shelf, jetty). Require at least 3 depth planes with parallax on every camera move.

issues.problem: The recurring X-ray column is drawn as a flat, saturated cyan UI panel with app-like icons. It clashes with the amber paper-cut world wherever it appears (ch11-s05, ch12-s01, ch12-s07, ch12-s08, ch13-s06, ch15-s04) and reads as a digital widget, not a theatre prop.
issues.fix: Redraw it as a backlit vellum or lightbox cabinet: paper grain, desaturated teal (around 40% saturation), cut-out band glyphs with soft glow, and a black cut-card frame that matches the Case Board.

issues.problem: Much in-scene text that carries meaning is too small to read at 1080p: Case Board cards, vertical candle labels, the ch05-s04 blame formula, the ch14-s05 47%/18% line, the ch15-s05 court rulings, the ch12-s06 'research preview' caption, the ch12-s08 user-estimate banner, and the ch08-s05 layer-size card.
issues.fix: Set a kit-wide minimum of about 22px cap height for any text the viewer must read. Push in whenever a card is the subject. Lay candle tags horizontally under the candle when the line names the candle.

issues.problem: The transformer reveal lands late and weak. 'every word looks at every other' (4.79-6.56s) plays over a near-black hall (darkBeat 3.78). allLight arrives at 7.32 on 'once', the threads are faint and run only from the first few slips, and the banner then covers most of the hall and shows blank for about 1s before it inks.
issues.fix: Move allLight to 'every' (4.79). Draw bright threads between every pair of slips along the whole hall, with all slips lit at once. Keep the banner small and low so it does not cover the slips, and ink it straight away on 'Transformer' (8.44).

issues.problem: In the final image, 'Somewhere tonight a lamp is on' (12.84s) plays over an almost black frame. The match strikes only after 'from' ends (18.88), and the candle catches at 20.04, so 'new candles' (17.30-18.21) lands on black. About 6s of black sits under the film's last spoken line.
issues.fix: Keep a dim, lit far window or lamp visible on 'lamp is on'. Bring the hand and matchbox in on 'suspicious' (15.2), strike on 'new' (17.30) and have the wick catch on 'candles' (17.74). Hold the lit candle afterwards.

issues.problem: The Go board is not 19x19 (about 14 lines), and the positions are decorative rings of stones, not a plausible game. Move 37 and move 78 are not at their real points. Go players will notice, and it undercuts the film's grounding.
issues.fix: Use a 19x19 board. Show the real Game 2 position near move 37, with the fifth-line shoulder hit on the right side ringed, and the real Game 4 wedge for move 78. A simplified stone count is fine, but stones must sit on intersections in a believable shape.

issues.problem: From 25:03 to 25:11 the frame is a full-screen blank cream ledger page while 'FTX' types in one letter at a time, and the Amazon/Google lines arrive only at 20.7s. It looks like a placeholder card: no depth, no silhouette, no light source.
issues.fix: Stage the ledger as an object on the desk under the lamp, with the hand, pen shadow and Case Board edge in frame. Write the FTX row on 'Five hundred million' and the Amazon/Google rows on 'billions', with no blank hold.

issues.problem: 'But America employed the most' (5.06-6.85s) has no visible payoff: the threads fan out to both shores symmetrically, the scholar figures and the 'CHINA 47% · US 18%' line are tiny, and an unspoken Qwen/Llama tag adds clutter in an 11s shot.
issues.fix: Enlarge the plate. On 'work' (5.26), visibly swing most threads from the right shore to the left, so the left-shore lanterns brighten and outnumber the right. Drop the Qwen tag or move it to ch14-s07.

issues.problem: In the backpropagation deep dive the loom fills only about 40% of the frame. The blame formula card is a thumbnail at the right edge and the per-knob tugs are too small to read, so the film's most important mechanism is seen from too far away.
issues.fix: Push in to about 70% frame fill from 'messenger' (16.83) to 'blame' (23.98). Double the formula card's size and place it beside the loom. Show each knob's tug as a visible rotation with a small +/- tick, at word anchors 'lantern by lantern' (20.37/21.05).

issues.problem: For about 11s a static wide shot of the Case Board runs while L1527 lists 'rules / knowledge / learning / data, fire, a messenger'. The highlights are pinpoints at this scale.
issues.fix: Make short camera pushes to each card on its word: 'rules' 6.34, 'knowledge' 7.74, 'Learning' 9.93, 'data' 11.77, 'fire' 12.49, 'messenger' 13.36, 'people' 14.52. Then pull back for 'Never one person'.

issues.problem: The 'research preview' caption is small low-contrast monospace on dark, and the first-note card ('plausible-sounding but incorrect') is cropped at the right edge of the frame around 24:28.
issues.fix: Keep the note card fully inside the safe area and enlarge it. Raise the caption's contrast and size.

issues.problem: The parrot's shuffled word strips cross the standing woman's silhouette (23:36-23:42), so two layers collide and the figure reads as cluttered.
issues.fix: Keep the word strips in front of the parrot perch on a separate plane, clear of the figure, or move the figure further right.

issues.problem: The scaling law is ruled as a descending line (loss falls), then match-cuts to an ascending skyline. The direction flips without explanation, and the axes are unlabelled except 'log scale'.
issues.fix: Label the axes (compute → / error ↓), or let the skyline step down left to right to match the line before the camera tilts to the towers.

issues.problem: The lettering on the struck match ('COMPUTE MATTERS LESS?') is unreadable, and the leftmost candle is cropped by the frame edge.
issues.fix: Push in on the match for its 1.4s life and enlarge the lettering. Reframe so the shelf's candles sit inside the frame.

issues.problem: The new gap candle, 'THE GAP IS MONTHS, NOT YEARS', is almost lost in the fog, which washes out the candle and its label.
issues.fix: Lower the haze in front of the candle, add a warm pool on the water beneath it, and raise the label's contrast.

issues.problem: It is hard to tell which of about 12 identical candles is the Cyc taper when it goes out on 'thirty-nine years'.
issues.fix: Rack focus or push in on the Cyc taper during 'out' (2.66), and keep its tag horizontal and readable.

issues.problem: The SOURCES end card says only 'published with the film', which reads as a placeholder. The first frame shows an empty grey rectangle, and blank parchment cards appear between text cards.
issues.fix: Put the actual sources location or a short-link on the card. Crossfade straight between text cards instead of through blank card stock.

issues.problem: The opening second (tilt) is murky empty teal panels before the study resolves.
issues.fix: Start the tilt on a readable element (the box or the X-ray band) or shorten the transition.

best_moments: ch02-s02: the paper-lantern threshold, which fills to the dashed line and fires, then splits into AND/OR with ink truth tables. It teaches the idea through the look.
ch03-s04: the Mark I in lab green, from the photocell eye to the harp of wires and the knob grid, with a live 'presentation 94 · mistakes in the last 20: 0' counter. Legible, period-true and moving.
ch10-s06: the attention worked example: scores 2·0·4·2 halved, one jug poured into cups, 'bank now means water 0.53'. The clearest mechanism plate in the film.
ch15-s01: the Nobel hall, with chandeliers, arched windows, a packed silhouette audience and the medallion turning toward Hopfield. The closest match to the reference frame's craft.
ch15-s07: Widrow's paper lantern on a snowy sill under the moon, with 'I never got over it.' Restrained and moving.
ch12-s06: the little lit box goes amber and swings open like a door, and the camera pulls back to one warm window in a cyan city. A strong visual rhyme with the cold open.
ch13-s02: Hinton walks from the centre of the light to its rim, where a pale ghost of his 1976 self is sitting.
ch06-s06: the messenger halves along a chain of lanterns (1, 0.5, 0.25 ... 0.0005), then the LSTM pipe carries it at full strength to step 1,029.
